decisions.title: Adventure — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The author states this is a conversion of Joel D. Park's existing commented disassembly and adds essentially no new analysis; do not count the conversion as an independent reverse-engineering project.

decisions.title: Super Mario Bros. — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The author ports doppelganger's existing disassembly and says he has not meaningfully modified the original analysis. Pattern-table visualizers are useful but this is not a separate original game disassembly.

decisions.title: Applesoft BASIC — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The ROM collection identifies this as a conversion of Bob Sander-Cederlof's pre-existing S-C Documentor disassembly; the converted listing is not counted separately. His underlying work remains a potential independent lead.

decisions.title: Super Serial Card firmware — manual conversion
decisions.reason: The ROM index explicitly describes the SourceGen SSC listing as ported from Apple's published firmware source in the installation manual, rather than a separate reconstruction.

decisions.title: Selected Apple II monitor ROMs — published-listing conversions
decisions.reason: The original, autostart, unenhanced IIe and original 16KB IIc monitor listings are described as faithful SourceGen reproductions of published Apple sources with little added commentary. This does not cover James Lewis's expanded 32KB IIc work, independent monitor analysis elsewhere, or James Davis's separate full-ROM project.

decisions.title: Apple IIe 80-column firmware — manual conversion
decisions.reason: The listing says its labels and comments come from Apple's published 80-Column Firmware Listing and describes itself as a fairly direct translation, so this SourceGen copy is not a separate original disassembly.

decisions.title: Apple II DOS 3.3 original-source archive
decisions.reason: Listed under original source listings in the SourceGen outbound index. The repository preserves original DOS 3.3 source and reference material; inspect its own annotations before claiming a distinct reverse-engineering project.

decisions.title: Robotron: 2084 (Atari 7800) — imported disassembly
decisions.reason: The listing's header attributes the Atari 7800 disassembly to Dan Boris with additional work by Scott T, while the enclosing repository documents a separate Apple II Robotron project. Resolve the credited original author's current source before cataloguing a canonical Atari 7800 research record.

decisions.title: jotd666/berzerk
decisions.reason: The sole Berzerk Z80 listing credits Scott Tunstall as its reverser, and the fuller canonical ScottTunstall/Berzerk repository is available. JOTD’s copied file has no independently evidenced Amiga translation; follow the original author for this arcade analysis.

decisions.title: jotd666/super_pacman
decisions.reason: Project-specific 6809 disassembly qualifies as arcade analysis. The README describes Mappy and the Amiga makefile references a missing super_pacman.68k, so no Super Pac-Man Amiga port or working build is claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/digdug
decisions.reason: Copied Dig Dug II README is superseded by the game-specific Dig Dug Z80 listing and Amiga assembly, with build/playability still unknown.

decisions.title: jotd666/rolling_thunder
decisions.reason: Copied Jail Break README does not describe this repository, but dual 6809/MCU listings, a distinct Rolling Thunder Amiga driver and TODO justify a work-in-progress record without build or playability claims.

decisions.title: jotd666/tiger_heli
decisions.reason: Project-specific Z80 disassembly qualifies as arcade analysis. README describes Jail Break, Amiga code describes Commando and makefile Dig Dug 2; no Tiger Heli Amiga port is claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/bosconian
decisions.reason: Copied Rally-X README is superseded by Bosconian Z80 listing and Bosconian-specific Amiga driver work; no playable port claim.

decisions.title: jotd666/mrdo
decisions.reason: Copied Jail Break README is superseded by Mr. Do! Z80 listing and Amiga-specific sprite/high-score code; predecessor template remains acknowledged.

decisions.title: jotd666/jungle_king
decisions.reason: A 256 KB Z80 listing and post-processing script qualify as an arcade disassembly; repository has no Amiga code, so an Amiga conversion is not claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/jrpacman500
decisions.reason: The 15 KB screenshot-to-68000-data conversion script is concrete Amiga development tooling, but the repository has only an assets directory and no generated src tree, game source or working build.

decisions.title: jotd666/marble_madness_2
decisions.reason: A 27 KB C RAM-dump renderer and graphics conversion script qualify as arcade video analysis. The Amiga slave and TODO lack completed ROM patching and tile/sprite ripping, so the record does not claim a playable Amiga port.

decisions.title: jotd666/amitools
decisions.reason: Fork of existing Amiga tools; no distinct JOTD reverse-engineering work established.

decisions.title: jotd666/mame
decisions.reason: MAME fork; no standalone Amiga/ST reconstruction demonstrated.

decisions.title: jotd666/Musashi
decisions.reason: 68000 emulator fork; review upstream rather than cataloguing an unverified duplicate.

decisions.title: jotd666/musashi040
decisions.reason: 68000 emulator fork; review upstream rather than cataloguing an unverified duplicate.

decisions.title: jotd666/gods-deluxe
decisions.reason: Primary Gods Deluxe README documents a substantial beta behavioral remake of the Amiga/Sega game, including observed differences and incomplete level coverage.

decisions.title: jotd666/supercars3
decisions.reason: Project readme.txt documents a substantial playable Super Cars I/II remake and original circuits with known AI/physics differences.

decisions.title: jotd666/pbmplus
decisions.reason: General image utility suite, not a distinct Amiga/ST reverse-engineering target.

decisions.title: jotd666/misctools
decisions.reason: README describes general-purpose Python home/work command-line scripts; grepbin alone does not establish a distinct Amiga/ST research project.

decisions.title: BLACK ICE — original Atari STE game
decisions.reason: Project-specific README explicitly says BLACK ICE is original homebrew built using lessons from the workspace, not a reconstruction or reverse-engineering project. Its Hatari-tested 1 MB STE target is useful development context but does not warrant a catalogue entry.

decisions.title: Into The Eagle’s Nest — misattributed Amiga/Atari ST entry
decisions.reason: The second catalogue entry described this same repository as a partial Amiga/Atari ST reconstruction. Its README and 68000 source establish only an Amiga disassembly. Merged the duplicate into the existing Amiga record and removed the unsupported Atari ST attribution.

decisions.title: The Air Dirt Demo
decisions.reason: README identifies full original assembler source for the group’s own 1996 Falcon demo, with no binary-to-source recovery claim.

decisions.title: The Ultimate Fake
decisions.reason: README identifies full assembler source for the group’s own 1998 ST demo; original-source publication does not itself establish reconstruction.

decisions.title: Xmas Card 97
decisions.reason: README identifies full assembler source for the group’s own 1997 Falcon demo, without a disassembly/reconstruction claim.

decisions.title: ST Floormat
decisions.reason: README identifies the original source and an old source version of the group’s own demo; the Falcon hardware requirement is not evidence of reverse engineering.

decisions.title: Dadplazz
decisions.reason: README identifies full original Falcon demo source and documented build instructions; no binary-to-source reconstruction is described.

decisions.title: RAWTex — planned Amiga/ST planar support
decisions.reason: README says Amiga and Atari ST planar export is planned, while current indexed chunky output primarily targets other architectures; revisit if support lands.

decisions.title: ProTrekkr
decisions.reason: Maintained modern music tracker and heavily modified NoiseTrekker derivative, but README does not establish a distinct Amiga/ST reverse-engineering subject or core disassembly/debugging tool.

decisions.title: STTRANS Atari ST-Book transfer research
decisions.reason: Original STTRANS.PRG, Ghidra project and substantive Python serial companion provide concrete STBook transfer protocol work; no reconstructed executable is claimed.

decisions.title: Starflight Atari ST analysis
decisions.reason: Ghidra project and BTX, AGO and OMEGA Python asset readers substantiate Atari ST binary and format analysis, without claiming a playable Starflight rebuild.

decisions.title: Think & Work Atari ST original-source port
decisions.reason: Author explicitly describes writing this Atari ST game from scratch from the Atari XL game levels and publishing its own original 68k source. No reverse-engineered binary or recovered-source work is established.

decisions.title: TurboAss Atari ST assembler original source
decisions.reason: Publishes the author’s original Atari ST assembler, editor and debugger source rather than independent recovery of a binary or a reconstructed legacy codebase.

decisions.title: AtariDocumentation official manual conversions
decisions.reason: Transcriptions and OCR/text conversions of Atari documentation. This is a document source archive rather than an independent software reverse-engineering subject.

decisions.title: Atari_ST_Sources original-source archive
decisions.reason: Large collection of existing Atari ST assembly and C source trees. The archive alone does not establish a distinct binary-to-source reconstruction project; review a specific contained project separately if authored reverse-engineering evidence appears.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/4489_byteloader
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this as a fork of 4489/4489_byteloader; copied README credits upstream and does not establish a separately documented disassembly. The Infinite Dreams README cites this loader in its later single-disk adaptation.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/amigaprogramming
decisions.reason: Original Amiga 68000 programming examples, without a documented recovered historic binary or reverse-engineered target.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/TTEDiskBuilder-netcore
decisions.reason: README identifies a .NET Core port of h0ffman’s existing ADF disk builder for VS Code; a useful development utility, but no separate reconstructed historical format or subject analysis is demonstrated.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/modprocessor
decisions.reason: Modern ProTracker sample recompression experiment for the author’s demo adaptation; README describes an untested original support utility, not a historic binary or format reconstruction.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/HardwareKeyboardReader
decisions.reason: README describes new Amiga 500 hardware keyboard library code and an in-progress VS Code example, not a reverse-engineered legacy software subject.

decisions.title: Championship Manager 93 folder
decisions.reason: Championship Manager 93 folder contains a game executable/data and patched binary but no distinct source reconstruction or analysis code. The documented Italia reconstruction is already catalogued; a second project for this binary folder would misstate its evidence.

decisions.title: DELA Eprommer reverse engineering
decisions.reason: Primary work reconstructs an Amiga expansion peripheral circuit and PAL equations, while its CLI is newly written to operate that hardware. It does not reconstruct legacy software within the tracker’s software-archaeology scope.

decisions.title: Tearaway Thomas partial reimplementation
decisions.reason: Packed/unpacked dumps and the Python DHp2 unpacker substantiate Amiga game data analysis; broader playability or full game reconstruction is not claimed.

decisions.title: cyxx/another_js
decisions.reason: The browser engine interprets Another World VM opcodes with DOS game data; promoted under DOS origin. Its Amiga palette option alone does not establish Amiga disk compatibility.

decisions.title: cyxx/hode
decisions.reason: A substantial Heart of Darkness engine reimplementation uses Windows demo/CD resource files; promoted under the Windows source platform without an Amiga or Atari ST claim.

decisions.title: nitecrwl
decisions.reason: Author labels the Atari ST game decompiled; gameplay C++, GEM AES/VDI code and cross-build Makefile substantiate source recovery. Original binary identity, matching and runtime verification remain unknown.

decisions.title: amiga_reconstructed
decisions.reason: Three named Amiga intros/trainers from this collection are already catalogued. Remaining directories have not been individually matched to a specific binary or reviewed for distinct reconstruction code; defer only those unexamined components rather than the entire collection.

decisions.title: amigaos-kickstart-source-history
decisions.reason: Surviving original AmigaOS RCS revisions were restored into a browsable Git timeline. This is source-history restoration within the preservation scope; it is not a ROM-derived reconstruction. Version tags and chronology are approximate.

decisions.title: ActionReplayAmiga
decisions.reason: Reverse engineered Action Replay hardware schematics and PAL/FPGA plans; hardware analysis rather than software or firmware reconstruction for the catalogue.

decisions.title: MidiMaze2
decisions.reason: Repository README offers historical shareware archives, disk images and screenshots, without source reconstruction or RE work in the repository.

decisions.title: STOS
decisions.reason: Original and adapted STOS BASIC interpreter/compiler assembly trees qualify as historical Atari ST development tooling. No binary-derived reconstruction or verified modern end-to-end build is claimed; component provenance remains open.

decisions.title: Amberstar original-source archive
decisions.reason: Original incomplete tokenized GFA Assembler development source archive, per its README. Preserve as provenance for Amberstar without treating it as a reverse-engineered reconstruction.

decisions.title: Boulder Dash modern Amiga clone
decisions.reason: New Amiga clone with editor; no primary evidence of recovered code or historical file-format analysis.

decisions.title: Pushover browser port (DOS-derived)
decisions.reason: Static and DOSBox analysis of Pushover DOS executables produced a browser game recreation using DOS data; promoted under DOS origin without asserting Amiga/ST binary or asset analysis.

decisions.title: The Faery Tale Adventure original Amiga sources
decisions.reason: Repository explicitly publishes original Amiga Aztec C/68000 source rather than a reverse-engineered reconstruction. Valuable historical source archive, but outside a distinct RE record.

decisions.title: Exploring Another World — DOS data research
decisions.reason: Concrete Haskell MEMLIST.BIN and BANK parsers qualify as DOS resource analysis. Referencing an Amiga ADF as background does not demonstrate decoding it.

decisions.title: Rockford Patcher — DOS target
decisions.reason: The patcher changes PC Rockford executable and data to recover hidden levels; promoted under DOS only. Historical Amiga art comparisons do not demonstrate Amiga binary patching.

decisions.title: L-Packer — source pending
decisions.reason: Documented and distributed beta packs Amiga and Atari ST executables, qualifying as directly relevant development tooling. Source is promised for a later release and is absent now; source audit and reproducible build are unknown.

decisions.title: Amiga smbfs — upstream protocol reverse engineering
decisions.reason: Amiga SMBFS is a port of Sharity-Light SMB filesystem code. The cited reverse engineering concerns SMB network protocol behavior, while this repository does not analyze a retro Amiga disk, application, executable, or game format; an ordinary native filesystem port alone falls outside the catalogue’s archaeology/tooling scope.

decisions.title: A2232 firmware historical source archive
decisions.reason: Archive contains original Commodore-era sources, including A2232 card firmware, rather than a reconstructed binary or new analysis project.

decisions.title: image-rider STX parser
decisions.reason: The example can extract STX track and sector data and the source implements parser scaffolding. README says formats are not fully parsed; included strictly as exploratory STX tooling.

decisions.title: FujiBoink Amiga conversion
decisions.reason: Atari ST demo to Amiga conversion includes Amiga assembly and asset-generation scripts. Included as a native port, without a binary-derived decompilation claim.

decisions.title: glfrontier FrontierVM 3
decisions.reason: FrontierVM 3 is a later experimental OpenGL renderer in Tom Morton’s existing FrontierVM/Atari ST Frontier lineage, already catalogued as frontier-vm-atari-st. External fe2.s game data and an incomplete renderer limit playability, but neither is a reason to defer a separate discovery decision.

decisions.title: albank1 Agent USA
decisions.reason: The collection lists Agent USA in its README but the tree contains only agentusa.prg, with no Agent USA assembly listing, parser or analysis source to catalogue as an independent reconstruction.

decisions.title: mist64/c64ref
decisions.reason: A curated reference collection and web presentation of ROM listings/memory maps by multiple historical authors. No distinct new binary reconstruction or original parser is established for this repository; the separately buildable c64rom project is catalogued.

decisions.title: Pokefinder-org/final_cartridge_3_original
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this repository as a fork of mist64/final_cartridge, the canonical reconstructed cartridge source added in this batch; no separately evidenced original work was identified.

decisions.title: unorig/DrWhoandtheMinesofTerror
decisions.reason: Repository currently contains only a Markdown item list; the description claims reverse-engineered C64 code, but no source, parser, or reproducible analysis artifact is present.

decisions.title: Piddewitt/C64-Game-Source-Code
decisions.reason: This repository is an index README linking the author’s separate game repositories, with no game source tree of its own; the linked original game studies are already catalogued individually.

decisions.title: g0me3/fceux
decisions.reason: This is a fork of TASEmulators/fceux described only as an Oregon Trail emulator. The current repository description does not establish whether it contains a distinct debugging, analysis or preservation contribution; compare the fork diff and locate project-specific documentation before deciding whether it warrants an independent record.

decisions.title: Crossroads II — old hyphz link
decisions.reason: The January 2025 article cites this old GitHub path; GitHub resolves the repository to MarkRdgOx/crossroads-2-disassembly, already tracked as crossroads2-c64-markrdgox.

decisions.title: Populous C/SDL2 fork
decisions.reason: Fork adds partial C translation but couples it to a game-specific SDL2 Amiga hardware layer, and many game routines remain stubs. Execution boundaries and distinct usable output need an audit before any promotion under the current game-specific-emulation exclusion.

decisions.title: AMSDOS ROM listing in Amstrad-ROM-Sources
decisions.reason: The directory README says the author's own initial work was abandoned and the completed disassembly is an unidentified predecessor's work copied for discoverability; no distinct analysis by this repository is demonstrated for AMSDOS.

decisions.title: GuillianSeed/MetalGear
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes a fully annotated MSX2 disassembly and reproducible Japanese/English ROM builds with expected CRC32 values.

decisions.title: mcolom/arkanoid_msx_disasm
decisions.reason: The annotated source documents z80dasm provenance, a z80asm rebuild command and the expected rebuilt-ROM SHA-1.

decisions.title: ValleyBell/PC98VNResearch
decisions.reason: The collection provides original PC-98 engine/game format research, tools, IDA material and rendered 16-bit x86 disassemblies rather than only links or binary assets.

decisions.title: FuzionCD/lime-juice
decisions.reason: Current C++ compiler/decompiler and image round-trip suite provides substantive PC-98 bytecode/data archaeology tooling with explicit supported and unsupported boundaries.

decisions.title: tomyun/juice
decisions.reason: lime-juice explicitly identifies this Racket implementation as its predecessor and carries the same Juice MES-tool lineage forward; it is retained as relationship evidence rather than a second catalogue record.

decisions.title: nmlgc/ReC98
decisions.reason: Primary documentation describes a maintained source reconstruction of Touhou 1–5 whose rebuilt PC-98 executables remain bit-perfect on every commit.

decisions.title: nmlgc/np2debug
decisions.reason: This Neko Project II fork documents a substantial debugger feature set built specifically for modification and translation of PC-98 binaries.

decisions.title: sidneycadot/Atari8bit_OSB-NTSC-ROM
decisions.reason: This is a substantive OCR/proofreading source-restoration and verified ca65 ROM-reconstruction workflow, not an ordinary original-source mirror.

decisions.title: fa8ntomas/blck-game-engine
decisions.reason: Although the README is only a title, the repository's primary engine.asm is a substantial project-specific annotated 6502 disassembly of Bruce Lee and Atari hardware behavior; unknown build/provenance facts remain explicitly unknown.

decisions.title: milnak/atari-vcs-disassembly
decisions.reason: The root is an aggregate of game sources and submodules, including credited third-party work, rather than one independently authored reconstruction. Individual canonical components require separate deduplication and review.

decisions.title: Dalekamistoso/MSXDUMPTOOLS
decisions.reason: The repository is a redistribution bundle of separately authored MSX utilities and assigns rights to their respective owners; it is useful as a discovery node but not a distinct development project.

decisions.title: radareorg/radare2
decisions.reason: General-purpose multi-platform reversing framework; the README gives no distinct legacy-platform project or extension to track here.

decisions.title: fcambus/jsemu
decisions.reason: Curated index of JavaScript emulators; useful for targeted discovery, but not an authored emulator itself.

decisions.title: VelocityRa/awesome-game-file-format-reversing
decisions.reason: Large curated game-format/resource index; useful as a source, not a standalone analysis tool.

decisions.title: alfishe/amiga-bootcamp
decisions.reason: Amiga development and internals reference, rather than an implemented retro software or analysis tool.

decisions.title: sf2000-qpsx-playstation-emulator
decisions.reason: Consumer PlayStation emulation port for SF2000/GB300; no project-specific recovery or source-debugging function established.

decisions.title: alphaSeclab/awesome-reverse-engineering
decisions.reason: Broad security/reverse-engineering link compilation dominated by modern platforms, not a distinct retro-development project.

decisions.title: danluu/debugging-stories
decisions.reason: General debugging-story link index; its incidental C64 link is not an authored retro software project.

decisions.title: Two9A/c64clicker
decisions.reason: Original browser-based incremental game with a C64 emulator, without documented legacy-software reconstruction or a reusable retro-development tool.

decisions.title: pong-wars
decisions.reason: Small original binary-only visual simulation inspired by a modern web toy; no original-software archaeology or substantial conversion established.

decisions.title: ZX-spectrum-512K-cartridge-Droy-
decisions.reason: Instructions for running an older third-party Windows cartridge creator in a VM; no authored cartridge/tool reconstruction in this repository.

decisions.title: Bread80/Amstrad-CPC-Kicad-Symbols
decisions.reason: KiCad hardware pinout symbols for CPC ICs; no software analysis or developer tool is implemented here.

decisions.title: oldschoolengine2
decisions.reason: Game-specific C64 compatibility engine for recent Covert Bitops titles; assess its execution path and relationship to the games before a catalogue record.

decisions.title: oldschoolengine2-emscripten
decisions.reason: Web/C++ port of the same game-specific engine; assess alongside the Unity implementation rather than counting as a separate game reconstruction.

decisions.title: amigavision/TopazDouble
decisions.reason: Hand-redrawn Amiga font assets; the README expressly says the font file format was not reverse engineered.

decisions.title: jbilander/SimpleDevice
decisions.reason: Amiga device-driver example/template with optional generated objdump output; no legacy-software recovery or standalone analysis tool.

decisions.title: na103/ar3
decisions.reason: Action Replay III hardware schematic reproduction, GAL programming files and ROM binaries; no published debugger source reconstruction.

decisions.title: pararaum/amigaexamples
decisions.reason: Amiga assembly tutorials and a mixed link list; useful for discovering upstream tools and analyses, not a single recovery project.

decisions.title: schlae/amiga-hddlw
decisions.reason: Reverse-engineered third-party Amiga HD floppy-drive adapter hardware and PAL logic; no floppy software or media-analysis tool.

decisions.title: AmstradGameDevChallenge/rpg-adventure
decisions.reason: Original CPC BASIC/C homebrew game and sprite-design examples; cited BASIC disassembly is a third-party reference, not project-specific archaeology.

decisions.title: muckypaws/AmstradCPC
decisions.reason: Mixed archive of period CPC sources, tools and commercial work; components need individual attribution and scope before promotion.

decisions.title: Amiga-68K-BobrHopper
decisions.reason: Port of the author’s new game to AmigaOS using offline sprite baking; no historical-game binary research or reusable analysis tool.

decisions.title: openttd_amiga_68k

decisions.title: Couch-To-64k---Breadboard-Z80-Computer
decisions.reason: Original Z80 breadboard computer tutorial and schematics; no legacy-software reconstruction or separate analysis tool.

decisions.title: CPC_Keyboards

decisions.title: CPC_ZERO
decisions.reason: Hypothetical new 6502 CPC-like computer based on inspiration from a prototype PCB, not a reconstruction of its software.

decisions.title: CPCModular
decisions.reason: CPC-compatible modular hardware and small test ROM/assembly snippets; no separately implemented CPC software archaeology project.

decisions.title: GreenHAL

decisions.title: Soft968-Amstrad-Firmware-Manual
decisions.reason: Hyperlinked CPC firmware manual, useful to verify firmware/jumpblock semantics but not an implemented analysis tool.

decisions.title: z80-character-lcd

decisions.title: cadaver.github.io

decisions.title: hid2ami

decisions.title: network-tester---pico-w5500
